title: Customer FAQ (Draft) — Buying Redwood Inference via AWS / GCP Cloud Marketplace
content:
NOTE: This is a customer-facing draft intended to be adapted into the docs site. Keep language precise; do not promise controls or timelines we can’t guarantee. Avoid “we are compliant with X” phrasing unless verified; link to the Security FAQ + share reports under NDA where needed.

Redwood Inference — Buying through AWS Marketplace / Google Cloud Marketplace
Customer FAQ (Draft)
Last updated: 2025-02-03

Who this is for
- Procurement, IT, and security teams who need to buy via AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace.
- Engineering teams who need to activate access quickly after purchase.

What you can buy via cloud marketplaces
Redwood Inference marketplace offers are organized to match common deployment needs:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Call the Redwood API from your application; metered usage billed through your cloud marketplace account.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): Reserved capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation (typically a committed monthly/annual amount).
- Private (VPC / on-prem options depending on offer): For regulated workloads and network isolation (sales-assisted; may require additional onboarding).
- Add-ons (where applicable): e.g., premium support/SLA, extended retention, compliance package.

Important: Not every SKU is available in every region or in the same packaging on AWS vs GCP. If you need a specific region, private offer structure, or invoice format, contact us before purchasing.

1) How does buying through a marketplace work?
In general:
1. You purchase Redwood Inference through AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace under your cloud billing account.
2. The marketplace sends Redwood an entitlement/subscription event.
3. You link the purchase to a Redwood organization (org) in the Redwood Console.
4. Redwood activates entitlements (plan + any add-ons) for that org, then you can start using the product.

If you already have a Redwood account/org:
- You can link the marketplace purchase to your existing org.

If you do not have a Redwood account:
- You’ll be prompted to create an org during the linking flow.

Typical activation time
- In most cases, entitlements activate within minutes after purchase.
- In some cases, activation can take longer due to marketplace processing delays or mismatches (account/org/region). If activation is not complete after ~30 minutes, see “Troubleshooting” below.

2) What do I need to provide to activate after purchase?
You will need:
- A Redwood user with admin access to the target Redwood org (or ability to create a new org).
- Your marketplace subscription/purchase identifier (AWS subscription ID or GCP entitlement ID) if requested by support.
- The cloud account/project that made the purchase (AWS payer account / GCP billing account and project).

For enterprise setups (Dedicated/Private), you may also need:
- Preferred region(s)
- Networking requirements (VPC, IP allowlists, PrivateLink/PSC if applicable)
- Security requirements (SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention)

3) Can I pay via PO / committed spend / invoicing through my cloud provider?
Yes—this is a common reason customers choose marketplace procurement.
- Your charges for Redwood via marketplace are billed through AWS or Google Cloud under your marketplace agreement.
- If your procurement team requires a private offer, committed spend structure, or specific invoice descriptors, contact Redwood Sales/Support before purchase.

4) How is pricing represented in the marketplace?
This varies by offer type:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Metered dimensions (e.g., tokens, embedding units, or request-based meters depending on the listing). Your marketplace bill reflects usage captured by Redwood’s metering.
- Dedicated / Private: Typically a contracted amount (monthly/annual) represented as a marketplace contract product or private offer.
- Add-ons: May appear as separate line items or included in a bundle depending on the listing.

Notes:
- Marketplace fees may affect list prices versus direct contracts.
- Discounting is often handled via private offers (not public list pricing).

5) How does usage metering work (Hosted API)?
For usage-based plans, Redwood reports usage to the marketplace metering service.
- Metering is based on your Redwood org’s usage tied to the marketplace entitlement.
- You can view usage and spend insights in the Redwood Console (token-level and request-level analytics) and compare to marketplace billing.

If you think metering is incorrect:
- Contact marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com with your Redwood org ID and the relevant date/time window.

6) Does marketplace purchase change my product experience?
Core product experience is the same. Differences are mainly in:
- Billing channel (marketplace vs direct)
- Entitlement activation / org linking step after purchase
- Some upgrade/downgrade flows (marketplaces have specific rules)

7) Can I move an existing direct contract to marketplace billing?
Often yes, but it depends on your current contract terms and the marketplace offer structure.
- Contact your Redwood account team (or marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com) and include:
  - Your Redwood org name
  - Current plan (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  - Desired marketplace (AWS or GCP)
  - Target start date

8) What is the upgrade/downgrade policy for marketplace plans?
Marketplaces have constraints on mid-term plan changes.
General guidance (exact steps depend on the offer):
- Hosted API (usage-based): You can usually add/remove add-ons by purchasing the corresponding add-on SKU (if available) and linking it to the same Redwood org.
- Dedicated / Private (contracted): Upgrades (more capacity, additional regions, premium SLA) typically require a private offer amendment or a new offer.
- Downgrades: Often take effect at renewal/end of term, or require a new offer.

If you need to change your plan:
- Contact Redwood (marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com) before making changes in the marketplace so we can ensure entitlements map cleanly to the correct org and prevent downtime.

9) Can we run in a specific region / meet data residency needs?
Redwood supports multiple regions, but availability depends on:
- The marketplace listing regions
- Your selected deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Any regulatory/security requirements

Guidance:
- Hosted API: You select from available regions supported by the API and your org policy.
- Dedicated/Private: Regions and residency requirements should be confirmed before purchase (often via a private offer).

For EU residency or regulated industry needs:
- Review the Security FAQ and contact Redwood for confirmation of your target region and controls.

10) What security documentation is available for marketplace reviews?
We provide a security FAQ tailored for marketplace buyers and can share additional evidence under NDA as appropriate.
Common requests:
- SOC 2 report handling (typically shared under NDA)
- Pen test attestation letter / summary
- Encryption overview (in transit / at rest) and key management options
- Audit logging overview
- Data retention options and deletion processes

Start here:
- Security FAQ: [LINK]
For formal security review:
- Email marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com and include your security contact + required timeline.

11) What is the shared responsibility model?
In short:
- Redwood is responsible for securing the Redwood service and platform controls in scope.
- You are responsible for securing your cloud account, user access to Redwood (e.g., SSO configuration if enabled), and how you use the service (e.g., what data you send and your internal policies).

Exact responsibilities vary by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). See the Security FAQ for details.

12) How do cancellations work?
Cancellation behavior depends on your marketplace and offer type:
- Usage-based: Typically you can stop usage at any time; marketplace subscription cancellation stops future usage being billed (note: there may be timing delays in marketplace systems).
- Contracted (Dedicated/Private): Cancellation terms typically follow the contract/private offer terms and marketplace rules.

If you cancel in the marketplace:
- Your Redwood entitlements will be removed after the marketplace processes the cancellation.
- To avoid service interruption, coordinate cancellation timing with your Redwood team.

13) Do you offer refunds?
Refunds are governed primarily by the marketplace’s refund policies and the specific offer terms.
- For usage-based plans, refunds are uncommon once usage has been consumed.
- For contracted offers, refunds (if any) follow the private offer/contract terms.

If you believe you were billed in error:
- Contact marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com with:
  - Marketplace (AWS or GCP)
  - Subscription/entitlement ID
  - Redwood org ID
  - Billing period and details of the issue

14) Are free trials or credits available via marketplace?
Sometimes, depending on the listing and marketplace capabilities.
- Marketplace structures vary; some trials/credits may be handled outside the marketplace.
- If you need a trial period for procurement reasons, contact Redwood and we will recommend the best path (marketplace trial vs direct evaluation).

15) How do add-ons work (premium SLA, extended retention, compliance package)?
If your marketplace offer includes add-ons:
- Add-ons map to entitlements within your Redwood org.
- Some add-ons may require configuration in the Redwood Console (e.g., retention settings) or a support-assisted enablement.

If you purchased an add-on but don’t see it in the Console:
- Wait a few minutes for entitlement propagation, then check the Marketplace/Entitlements page in the Console.
- If still missing, contact support with your entitlement ID.

16) What happens if multiple cloud accounts/projects purchase Redwood, but we want one Redwood org?
This is a common enterprise scenario.
- Redwood can support linking entitlements to the correct Redwood org, but it must be done carefully to avoid split billing or missing entitlements.

Recommendation:
- Before purchasing, decide which cloud billing account/project should own the subscription(s).
- If you need consolidation, contact Redwood support and include your intended mapping.

17) Troubleshooting activation issues
Common issues and fixes:
A) “I purchased but I don’t see entitlements in Redwood yet”
- Wait 10–30 minutes (marketplace processing delay can happen).
- Confirm you are logged into the intended Redwood org.
- Try the “Link marketplace purchase” flow again from the Console.

B) “Entitlement is linked to the wrong Redwood org”
- Do not attempt multiple re-links across orgs.
- Contact support; we can help correct mapping (may require verification).

C) “Region mismatch” or “offer not available in my region”
- Confirm the region selected in the marketplace matches what you intend to use.
- For Dedicated/Private, confirm region availability before purchase.

Information to include in support requests:
- Marketplace: AWS or GCP
- Marketplace subscription/entitlement ID
- Your cloud account/project (payer account ID or GCP project ID)
- Redwood org name + org ID (from Console)
- Timestamp of purchase and any error messages/screenshots

18) How do I contact support?
For marketplace-related questions (activation, billing mapping, entitlement issues):
- Email: marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com
- In-product: Redwood Console → Support (preferred if available)

For enterprise procurement help (private offers, SKU selection, terms):
- Contact your Redwood account team, or email marketplace-support@redwoodinference.com and we will route you.

Response expectations (draft; confirm with Support/CS):
- Best effort during business hours; severity-based escalation for active production impact.
